summary:
Weekly Overseer Digest

Issues Found
- overseer — GitHub token invalid: all read/search/file tools return `401 Bad credentials`. Overseer was fully blind this cycle and couldn't even file this bug itself. MANUAL FIX: rotate the PAT, verify scopes (repo read + issues write), then re-run to backfill the skipped crypto-trading / coachvision / ufc-dashboard checks. (The per-project "couldn't read" notes are all symptoms of this one root cause.)

Top Enhancement Ideas (ranked)
1. overseer — Credential preflight + graceful degradation (effort: low, impact: high): validate token at startup and normalize auth failures into structured "not_configured" payloads so one expired secret can't blind the whole pipeline — exactly today's failure.
2. crypto-trading — Structured daily run summary as JSONL (effort: low, impact: high): P&L, fills, slippage, equity, errors as a queryable time series; unlocks dashboards + backtesting.
3. overseer — Golden-file unit tests + CI for tracer/read-tool parsers (effort: low, impact: medium): catch schema drift before the weekly run.
4. overseer — Cache last-successful read snapshots, serve stale-with-timestamp on failure (effort: medium, impact: high): keeps reviews useful during outages/expired creds.
5. ufc-dashboard — Track odds movement with line-move / CLV alerts (effort: medium, impact: high): highest-value signal the scraper currently discards.
6. crypto-trading — Regime filter + volatility-scaled position sizing (effort: medium, impact: high): constant risk budget, better risk-adjusted P&L; backtestable on existing logs.
7. coachvision — Kalman/optical-flow ball-track interpolation + smoothing (effort: medium, impact: high): bridges detection gaps for cleaner trajectories, no retraining.

timeline.text_full: The GitHub token being expired is the root cause blocking everything—that's the critical bug to surface. The credential preflight idea and this bug are related but separate: one's about the immediate token failure, the other's about building resilience so the system doesn't completely break when credentials fail. I'll keep them distinct, with the bug as the top priority issue and the idea as an enhancement. For the enhancement ranking, I'm prioritizing by effort-to-impact ratio: credential preflight and the JSONL summary are quick wins with high payoff, followed by the golden-file tests, then the medium-effort items like caching snapshots and the other feature improvements. I'll drop the medium/medium fallback and high/high highlight reels since they're lower priority, keeping the list tight and scannable.
